sector_news.title: Indian pharma market grew 13.5% in September 2026 (12-month 10.9%); volume only +2.9%, so growth is coming from price and mix
sector_news.impact: Supports domestic-heavy names (Mankind, Alkem, Ipca, Ajanta). Volume-light growth = pricing & new launches matter more than reach.

statement_impact.pl: Market growth supports India revenues for all six.
statement_impact.doing: Companies outgrowing the market: Ajanta, Ipca, Glenmark.
statement_impact.should: Track share gains vs the market monthly, by therapy.

sector_news.title: US Section 232 100% tariff on patented drugs widens; India gets zero-duty eligibility for select specialty categories; generics excluded
sector_news.impact: Generic exporters (Alembic, Ajanta, Alkem, Glenmark US) largely outside scope. Specialty/branded (Alembic Pivya, Glenmark Ryaltris) need product-level review.

statement_impact.pl: Generics excluded for now; specialty brands may face tariffs.
statement_impact.doing: Indian firms rely on the generics exclusion.
statement_impact.should: Map each company's US product mix by tariff exposure.

sector_news.title: US President signals generics tariff path: 0% for 2 years from Aug-1, then 100%, then 200% for firms not building US plants
sector_news.impact: Medium-term overhang on US-heavy generics (Alembic 36% US, Ajanta 30%, Glenmark 27%, Alkem 20%). Triggers US-footprint / CDMO-partnering strategy questions.

statement_impact.pl: If applied, US margins fall sharply after 2 years unless companies build US plants.
statement_impact.doing: 0% for 2 years gives time to adapt.
statement_impact.should: US footprint options study: contract manufacturing, partner plants, price strategy.

sector_news.title: API, solvent & logistics inflation from Middle-East conflict flagged by Glenmark, Mankind, Alkem, Ipca on Q1 calls
sector_news.impact: Gross-margin pressure expected for 2+ quarters; backward-integrated players (Ipca, Alembic API) relatively insulated.

statement_impact.pl: Material and freight costs up, so gross margin falls.
statement_impact.cf: More cash tied up in stock.
statement_impact.doing: Flagged on Q1 calls; API-integrated firms (Alembic, Ipca) are cushioned.
statement_impact.should: Procurement and price-pass-through programme; dual sourcing.

meta.one_offs: Dr Reddy's and Cipla lost US lenalidomide (generic Revlimid) sales in FY26; Dr Reddy's FY26 includes a ₹450 Cr shelf-stock adjustment; Lupin's FY26 was lifted by limited-competition US products (tolvaptan, mirabegron) that face competition in FY27; Zydus growth includes acquisitions (Amplitude, Assertio); Sun's Organon deal (US$11.75 bn) is pending; Sun (Halol), Cipla (Pithampur), Lupin (Pithampur Unit II) and Aurobindo (Eugia Unit-I) have open US FDA issues.
regulatory_takeaways: Approvals are not revenue. Aurobindo has by far the biggest US book (737 approvals) but the lowest margin and returns of the six; Lupin earns a 30% margin from fewer, harder products. Picking limited-competition products beats volume.

R&D and margin (link strength {rr}): Zydus (8.4%), Lupin (7.5%) and Dr Reddy's (7.2%) spend the most. Lupin shows the payoff; Dr Reddy's shows the risk when a big product (lenalidomide) ends before the next wave arrives.

Four of six have an open US FDA issue: Sun (Halol OAI and import alert), Cipla (Pithampur warning letter, 7 new observations Aug 2026), Lupin (Pithampur Unit II OAI) and Aurobindo (Eugia Unit-I warning letter, Aug 2026). Quality is a growth constraint for the majors, not a one-company problem.

The lenalidomide cliff is visible in the numbers: Dr Reddy's North America fell 22% in FY26 and Cipla's US sales 28% in Q1 FY27, while Sun's US generics fell 9.7%. Biosimilars, GLP-1s and inhalers are the replacements.

companies.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries
companies.tagline: India's largest drugmaker, shifting from US generics to global innovative medicines, now buying Organon

profile.business_model: India branded formulations (#1, 8.5% share), global innovative medicines (dermatology, ophthalmology, onco-derma), US and emerging-market generics, API.
profile.description: Largest pharma company in India (8.5% share, MAT Jun 2026) and #1 by prescriptions across 12 specialist groups. Innovative medicines reached US$1.42 bn in FY26 (about 21% of sales). Net cash about ₹12,400 Cr before the US$11.75 bn Organon deal (announced Apr 2026, close expected Q4 FY27).

footprint.market: India #1 with 8.5% share (AIOCD MAT Jun 2026), 30 brands in India's top 300. #1 by prescriptions with psychiatrists, neurologists, cardiologists, gastroenterologists, diabetologists and dermatologists. 13th largest in US generics.
footprint.manufacturing: 40 sites: formulations in India (12), US (3), Bangladesh (2) and 10 other countries; API in India (8), Australia (2), Israel, US and Hungary. Halol (Gujarat) is OAI with the US FDA and under import alert.
footprint.rnd: FY26 R&D ₹3,554 Cr (6.1% of sales); Q1 FY27 5.4%, with 30% of R&D on innovative medicines. Pipeline: Leqselvi (alopecia), Unloxcyt (skin cancer), Ilumya, Odomzo; semaglutide launched in India and South Africa.
footprint.therapies_basis: India therapy mix (%), Sun investor presentation Sep 2026

regulatory.status: Halol: OAI after the Jun 2025 inspection (8 observations) and still under US import alert. NDAs: 70 filed, 57 approved, 13 pending. 13th largest in US generics.

companies.guidance: FY27: revenue growth in high single digits (reiterated after Q1); continued launch spend on Leqselvi and Unloxcyt; tax rate about 27.8% until Organon closes; Organon close expected in Q4 FY27.
data_notes: Organon (US$11.75 bn, about US$6.2 bn of sales) is not in these numbers; close expected Q4 FY27.
Q1 FY27 includes a ₹167 Cr exceptional charge for Organon deal costs.

problems.title: Integrate Organon and protect the balance sheet
problems.evidence: US$11.75 bn deal; Organon sales about US$6.2 bn, flat for four years; Nexplanon faces loss of exclusivity.
problems.answer: Integration office with a 100-day plan, synergy tracking by function, portfolio pruning of Organon's mature brands and a debt pay-down plan.
problems.investigate: Overlap by country and product; Nexplanon erosion curve; manufacturing network across Organon's six EU sites.
problems.service: Strategy: M&A integration and synergy capture

problems.title: Make innovative medicines pay back faster
problems.evidence: Innovative sales US$1.42 bn; Q1 FY27 EBITDA +2.7% only, as launch spend on Leqselvi and Unloxcyt rises.
problems.answer: Launch excellence: payer access, prescriber targeting and a stop-or-scale rule for each launch.
problems.investigate: Sales and spend per brand; payer coverage; prescriber growth curves.

problems.title: Plan for a shrinking US generics book
problems.evidence: US formulations US$427 M in Q1 FY27, down 9.7%; lenalidomide fading; 13th in US generics.
problems.answer: Portfolio triage: keep complex, differentiated generics; exit or out-license low-margin products; shift plant capacity.
problems.investigate: Product-level margin and erosion; plant loading by product.

problems.title: Clear Halol with the US FDA
problems.evidence: OAI after the Jun 2025 inspection (8 observations); still under import alert.
problems.answer: Quality remediation programme with data-integrity controls and independent readiness audits; move key US products to clean sites.
problems.investigate: Observation themes; product-to-site map; FDA timeline.

problems.title: Free cash from 363 days of inventory
problems.evidence: Inventory days rose from 315 (FY22) to 363 (FY26); cash cycle 228 days.
problems.answer: Inventory diagnostic by business, S&OP and SKU rationalisation; target 30 to 60 fewer days.
problems.investigate: Inventory by business and stage; SKU tail.

companies.name: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories
companies.tagline: Global generics and API player rebuilding growth after the US lenalidomide cliff, betting on semaglutide and biosimilars

profile.leadership: K. Satish Reddy (Chairman); G. V. Prasad (Co-Chairman and MD); Erez Israeli (CEO)
profile.business_model: North America generics, emerging markets, India branded, Europe (incl. acquired NRT brands), API and services (PSAI, Aurigene CDMO).
profile.description: FY26 revenue ₹33,594 Cr (+3.2%) as US lenalidomide (generic Revlimid) faded; North America fell 22%. Emerging markets (+23%), India (+16%) and Europe (+55% with NRT) grew. Net cash ₹3,270 Cr. Semaglutide launched in India (Obeda) and Canada; abatacept biosimilar FDA goal date 22 Dec 2026.
profile.employees_note: India rank #9 by quarter, #10 by year (IQVIA Mar 2026)

footprint.market: India #9 to #10 (IQVIA Mar 2026), 15 brands in India's top 300. North America is the largest market but shrinking without lenalidomide; Europe boosted by acquired nicotine-replacement (NRT) brands.
footprint.manufacturing: Formulation and API plants in India (Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam, Baddi), plus sites in the US, UK and Mexico. Aurigene CDMO earned over US$100 M in the 12 months to Sep 2026.
footprint.rnd: FY26 R&D ₹2,406 Cr (7.2% of sales, down 12%); guided back to 7 to 8%. Pipeline: semaglutide (India, Canada, 10 countries approved), abatacept biosimilar (FDA goal 22 Dec 2026), rituximab biosimilar (FDA approved), denosumab.
footprint.therapies_basis: Business mix (%); therapy split not disclosed

regulatory.status: 75 ANDAs pending (43 Paragraph IV) plus 2 NDAs (31-Mar-2026); 15 ANDAs filed in FY26. No plant-level FDA action disclosed in the Q2 FY27 call. Abatacept biosimilar goal date 22 Dec 2026.

companies.guidance: FY27: EBITDA margin 20%+ (freight and raw-material costs about 1 point drag); R&D 7 to 8% of sales; capex ₹1,600 to 1,700 Cr; semaglutide relaunch Nov 2026; abatacept FDA decision 22 Dec 2026.
data_notes: FY24 and FY25 were lifted by US lenalidomide (generic Revlimid) sales, which ended in FY26.
FY26 includes a ₹450 Cr one-time shelf-stock adjustment in North America; Q4 FY26 margin 5%.
Europe includes nicotine-replacement (NRT) brands acquired from Haleon.

problems.title: Reset the cost base for a smaller US business

problems.title: Scale emerging markets and India profitably

problems.title: Win the abatacept biosimilar launch

problems.answer: Launch plan with payer contracting and a backup timeline.

companies.name: Cipla
companies.tagline: India's respiratory leader with a debt-free balance sheet, rebuilding US growth through complex inhalers

profile.leadership: Y. K. Hamied (Chairman); Achin Gupta (MD and Global CEO since Apr 2026)
profile.business_model: One India (branded Rx, trade generics, consumer health), North America (complex generics, inhalers, peptides), South Africa and Africa, emerging markets and Europe, API.
profile.description: FY26 revenue ₹28,163 Cr; India about 45% (crossed ₹12,680 Cr). Respiratory leader: Foracort crossed ₹1,000 Cr. Net cash over ₹10,500 Cr. US hit by the end of lenalidomide and a lanreotide supply break; generic Advair (Jul 2026) and Ventolin approvals rebuild the inhaler pipeline.
profile.employees_note: R&D about 7% of revenue (nearly ₹2,000 Cr in FY26)

footprint.market: India is about 45% of sales; record India quarter of ₹3,452 Cr in Q1 FY27 (+12%), branded Rx +15.4%. Respiratory leader in India (Foracort above ₹1,000 Cr). US about 24% of sales.
footprint.manufacturing: Plants in India (Goa, Pithampur, Indore, Bengaluru, Patalganga, Kurkumbh), US (InvaGen, New York; Fall River) and Africa. Pithampur under FDA warning letter (Nov 2023); re-inspection Aug 2026 gave 7 observations. Goa, Bengaluru and Navi Mumbai VAI or NAI.
footprint.rnd: FY26 R&D nearly ₹2,000 Cr (about 7% of revenue). Pipeline: respiratory (generic Advair, Ventolin, Dulera), peptides (lanreotide), inhaled insulin partnership with MannKind.
footprint.therapies_basis: Indicative India mix (company commentary; exact split not disclosed)

regulatory.status: Pithampur: under US FDA warning letter (Nov 2023); re-inspection 17 to 25 Aug 2026 gave a Form 483 with 7 observations. Goa VAI; InvaGen (NY) 1 observation; Indore re-inspection due.

companies.guidance: FY27: EBITDA margin 18.5 to 20% (recovery weighted to H2); US exit run-rate of US$1 bn by end FY27 on complex launches (generic Advair, Ventolin).
data_notes: FY24 and FY25 were lifted by US lenalidomide (generic Revlimid) sales, which ended in FY26.

companies.name: Lupin
companies.tagline: The turnaround story: from a loss in FY22 to a 30% margin on US limited-competition launches, now facing the FY27 reset

profile.leadership: Manju D. Gupta (Chairperson); Vinita Gupta and Nilesh Gupta (CEO and MD)
profile.business_model: US generics and complex products (inhalers, injectables), India branded (8th in India), other developed markets incl. Europe (VISUfarma), emerging markets, API.
profile.description: FY26 sales ₹27,488 Cr (+23.9%), EBITDA margin 33.6% (company basis), PAT +62%. US +46% on tolvaptan and mirabegron. 3rd in the US by filled generic prescriptions; 444 ANDAs and NDAs filed. FY27 guided as a reset year as those products face competition.
profile.employees_note: India #8 (IQVIA MAT Mar 2026); 52 first-to-file US opportunities

footprint.market: India #8 (IQVIA MAT Mar 2026); chronic about 67% of India sales; diabetes +31.8% in Q1 FY27. US: 3rd by filled generic prescriptions, 151 generic products marketed.
footprint.manufacturing: Plants in India (Pithampur, Goa, Nagpur, Ankleshwar, Aurangabad) and the US (Somerset, Coral Springs). Pithampur Unit II is OAI with the US FDA; Ankleshwar and Somerset VAI.
footprint.rnd: FY26 R&D ₹2,063 Cr (7.5% of sales); Q1 FY27 7.4%; guided about 8% for FY27. Pipeline: 30+ injectables, 20+ respiratory products, biosimilars (ranibizumab), Dulera, apixaban new dosage form.
footprint.therapies_basis: Indicative India mix (chronic about 67%; exact split not disclosed)

regulatory.status: Pithampur Unit II: OAI, responses submitted and remediation in progress. Ankleshwar and Somerset: VAI (EIRs received). 444 ANDAs and NDAs filed in total; 52 first-to-file opportunities.

companies.guidance: FY27: high single-digit revenue growth; EBITDA margin about 25% (from 33.6%); US sales US$1.1 to 1.2 bn; R&D about 8% of sales; price pressure on tolvaptan and mirabegron from Q2 FY27.
data_notes: FY22 was a loss year (one-time charges and US price erosion).
FY26 was lifted by limited-competition US launches (tolvaptan, mirabegron) that face competition in FY27.
VISUfarma (Europe ophthalmology) consolidated from Q1 FY27.

companies.name: Aurobindo Pharma
companies.tagline: Largest US generics supplier by volume and a top-10 generic player in Europe, pushing into biosimilars and US manufacturing

profile.business_model: US formulations (orals and Eugia injectables), Europe generics, growth markets, ARV, API (beta-lactam heavy); biosimilars through CuraTeQ.
profile.description: FY26 revenue ₹33,653 Cr (+6.1%), EBITDA margin 20.4%. 896 ANDAs filed and 737 approved (Jun 2026), the largest book in India. Bought Lannett (US) for US$250 M in Jun 2026, adding about 4 bn doses of US capacity. Biosimilars approved in the EU, UK and Canada.
profile.employees_note: Top-10 generic company in 8 European countries

footprint.market: Little India branded business; a global generics model. US: the largest ANDA book from India. Europe: top-10 generic company in 8 countries; Europe grew 25.6% in Q1 FY27.
footprint.manufacturing: Many formulation and API sites in India (Hyderabad, Vizag, Telangana), Eugia injectables, Lannett (Seymour, Indiana) in the US, plus Europe. Eugia Unit-I got an FDA warning letter (Aug 2026, about 2% of revenue).
footprint.rnd: R&D about 4.5% of sales (Q4 FY26, incl. depreciation). Biosimilars (CuraTeQ): Zefylti, Dyrupeg, Dazublys approved in the EU; Bevqolva in the UK and Canada; denosumab and omalizumab filings.
footprint.therapies_basis: Business mix (% of FY26 sales); US split indicative

regulatory.status: Eugia Unit-I (Telangana): US FDA warning letter (Aug 2026), about 2% of group revenue; US supply continues. 896 ANDAs filed, 737 final and 33 tentative approvals (30-Jun-2026).

companies.guidance: No numeric FY27 guidance in the Q1 release. Goal of US$2 bn US revenue (Lannett adds controlled-substance capacity); biosimilars scaling in Europe.
data_notes: Lannett (US, acquired 29 Jun 2026 for US$250 M) is not in FY26 numbers.

companies.name: Zydus Lifesciences
companies.tagline: Diversified pharma with India brands, US generics, consumer wellness and medtech, buying its way into US specialty

profile.leadership: Pankaj R. Patel (Chairman); Dr. Sharvil Patel (Managing Director)
profile.business_model: US formulations (3rd among US generics by prescriptions), India branded, consumer wellness (Glucon-D, Nycil, Sugar Free, Complan), international markets, medtech (Amplitude Surgical), API; US specialty via Assertio.
profile.description: FY26 revenue ₹27,148 Cr (+16.8%), EBITDA margin 31.2% (company basis). Acquisitions: Amplitude Surgical (France, medtech), Assertio (US, US$166 M, Jun 2026). First US ranibizumab biosimilar (Nufymco). Moved from net cash to net debt (0.5x EBITDA).
profile.employees_note: India chronic share 46.3%; 10 India brands above ₹100 Cr

footprint.market: US: 3rd among US generic companies by prescriptions; India branded +15% in FY26 with chronic at 46.3%; consumer wellness #1 in Glucon-D, Nycil and Sugar Free.
footprint.manufacturing: Formulation, injectable and biologics sites in Gujarat (Ahmedabad, Zydus Biotech Park), plus US and international sites; Amplitude Surgical plants in France. Biotech Park injectables VAI after the Apr to May 2026 inspection.
footprint.rnd: FY26 R&D ₹2,273 Cr (8.4% of sales, highest of the six); Q1 FY27 8.0%. Pipeline: saroglitazar for PBC (FDA priority review), biosimilars (ranibizumab, nivolumab, aflibercept), a biosimilar ADC in Phase III.

regulatory.status: Zydus Biotech Park injectables: VAI after the Apr to May 2026 inspection. Saroglitazar (PBC) under FDA priority review, decision later in FY27. 9 ANDA approvals and 11 US launches in Q1 FY27.

companies.guidance: FY27: strong double-digit revenue growth; EBITDA margin 24%+; India branded mid-teens growth; US generics single-digit; 30 to 40 US launches; capex ₹1,500 to 1,600 Cr; EBITDA margin 28 to 30% by FY30.
data_notes: Acquired: Amplitude Surgical (medtech) in FY26, Assertio (US) from Q2 FY27, plus consumer acquisitions; part of growth is bought.
Screener's FY25 cost split did not reconcile, so FY25 cost shares are left blank.
FY26 includes a ₹398 Cr exceptional charge for the mirabegron litigation settlement.
